passages.text: Ren was born into a rural teaching family in Guizhou, studied civil engineering, then joined the PLA's Engineering Corps in 1974 to help build the Liaoyang Chemical Fiber Factory, rising to a deputy-regimental-equivalent technical role before the Corps was disbanded in 1983.

After leaving the military and working briefly for a Shenzhen oil-logistics company, Ren founded Huawei in September 1987 with registered capital of 21,000 yuan, reportedly out of dissatisfaction with his prior job.
Founded Huawei Technologies in Shenzhen in September 1987 as a private telecommunications equipment reseller/manufacturer.

Huawei grew into, per Wikipedia's characterization, the world's largest telecommunications equipment manufacturer and a top-tier global smartphone maker, with Ren remaining CEO nearly four decades later.

Ren has held the CEO title at Huawei continuously since 1988, and Wikipedia's infobox lists his Huawei vice-chairman tenure as running from the company's founding until November 2019, when Meng Wanzhou succeeded him in that vice-chair role.

Ren Zhengfei belongs to Group 2 - Reform-era pioneers. The reform-era pioneers group covers founders who built their businesses in the 1980s and 1990s opening of China's economy under Deng Xiaoping, spanning telecom equipment (Huawei), personal computing (Lenovo), home appliances (Haier), beverages (Wahaha), and automotive components (Wanxiang), often starting from township-enterprise or small-collective origins.
